name: Travelmanager – Tours, Tickets & Bookings
author: PHCOM GmbH

sections.description:
Turn website visitors into your next guests. Travelmanager brings tours, tickets and events straight to WordPress, helping customers discover their next experience and start booking.

Connect your booking system to WordPress. Showcase departures, guide visitors with Tour finder and calendars, and present experiences with inviting event cards. Add products and gift vouchers, and combine shortcode blocks with your own page design.

Manage schedules, products and bookings in your existing Travelmanager account. Compatible Gastrozack services retain their integrations. This plugin connects to an external service; it is not a standalone booking engine. An account is required. Charges, availability, privacy terms and service conditions depend on your provider.

Settings and languages

Settings → Travelmanager offers an optional default account, language selection and connection test. Explicit shortcode accounts always override the saved account. Existing pages work without new settings or tokens. The test checks the Travelmanager endpoint over HTTPS without creating a booking.

WordPress token (optional): copy the value from Travelmanager. With no stored token, existing unauthenticated requests continue. A configured token is stored encrypted and sent only server-side to xwordpress_endpoint.php on the saved account: GET uses the wordpress_token query parameter; POST uses an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body field. Existing call parameters and the historical XML/shortcode token parameter remain unchanged.

Travelmanager requires this token only when set.wordpress_token is configured; tenant ent_tm is exempt on the server. The plugin does not infer or bypass tenant rules. Missing/invalid credentials produce a clear authentication error (HTTP 403, INVALID_WORDPRESS_TOKEN). There is no automatic retry without the token and errors are not cached as successful data. The connection test uses the same endpoint and token; success on an exempt account does not prove token enforcement.

The saved token is never displayed in the form, shortcodes or browser code. A blank password input keeps a saved token; use Remove the stored token to return to an empty setting. Replace or remove it before changing the saved account. Explicit shortcodes for other accounts never receive that account’s private token.

Keep existing behavior is the default. Opt into Automatic to follow the page/site language, or select a fixed language. Supported codes: de (German), en (English), pl (Polish), cs (Czech), fr (French), es (Spanish), it (Italian), da (Danish), nl (Dutch). A supported lang overrides the new mode; regional locales are normalized and cz maps to cs.

In the new mode, backend-generated eventcalendar content uses German for de and English for all other languages, including AJAX. Plugin controls retain the selected language. Other calls request their selected language. Backend descriptions and hosted interfaces need the provider’s translations.

Content Bridge (optional)

Share your saved website text with the Travelmanager chatbot. In Settings → Travelmanager → Settings → Content Bridge, select Enable Content Bridge and save its separate form. The feature is off by default, including after an upgrade; a plugin version containing Content Bridge is required.

After saving, copy the displayed Content Bridge URL into the corresponding website-source setting in your Travelmanager chatbot. No shortcode is needed. The public, read-only WordPress REST endpoint is travelmanager/v1/content-bridge; always use the displayed URL, which also supports subdirectory installations and plain permalinks.

The endpoint returns one complete UTF-8 JSON array with these fields for every eligible page or post:

  • url: full page/post permalink.
  • title: saved title as plain text.
  • description: manually saved excerpt as plain text, or an empty string.
  • inhalt: saved editorial body as plain text, with line and paragraph breaks.

Only published, publicly viewable WordPress pages and posts without a password are included. Drafts, private or scheduled content, attachments and custom post types are excluded. WordPress’s site-wide search-engine indexing restriction returns an empty array. Stored noindex settings from Yoast SEO, Rank Math and SEOPress are also respected, including supported post-type/global defaults. Custom SEO, theme-only robots rules or membership restrictions need a site-specific integration; actual search-engine indexing is not checked.

The export reads saved editorial content without rendering the page. It removes HTML markup, shortcodes and their enclosed content, plugin blocks, dynamic queries/embeds, synced-block references and bound block content. Saved core text blocks, headings, lists, tables and captions retain their text and order. TM-generated timetables, calendars, booking interfaces and other plugin results are not included. A shortcode-only page can therefore have an empty inhalt. Text stored only in pagebuilder custom fields or shortcode-based builder containers is not exported.

When enabled, the export is publicly accessible without a WordPress login or the private Travelmanager WordPress token. Enabling it does not automatically send text to Travelmanager or another service. The chatbot imports the URL when you explicitly update its knowledge there. Disabling the bridge immediately returns HTTP 404; it does not remove an earlier chatbot import. Refresh the chatbot’s knowledge separately after changing its sources.

The plugin does not cache export responses and sends no-store headers. Exclude this REST route from any page/CDN cache that overrides those headers. When the site has no eligible content, the response is [].

Shortcode basics

Use a WordPress Shortcode block. Replace example IDs with IDs from your account. Every call needs an explicit or saved account:

[travelmanager call="timetable" account="example.travelmanager.software" station_id="2" max="12"]

With a saved account, omit account. Empty/omitted call selects timetable; existing technical aliases remain supported. Do not translate attribute names: use linie_id and linie_typ_id.

Attribute reference

Most attributes default to empty. They affect only calls that implement them. Use literal true/false, not 1/0.

  • account: backend hostname; explicit value overrides settings.
  • call: view identifier; default timetable.
  • lang: language override in the opt-in mode; legacy precedence stays unchanged.
  • vermittler_id: numeric referral; existing URL/session referral handling remains.
  • cache: false bypasses the plugin’s API read cache, not page/CDN caches.
  • station_id: station filter; timetable accepts comma-separated IDs.
  • linie_id: timetable/route-calendar route ID; timetable also accepts ID lists.
  • linien_ids: Tour finder route IDs, comma-separated; not a universal filter.
  • linie_typ_id: route category/type IDs, comma-separated where supported.
  • category_id: shop category, distinct from route type.
  • product_id: catalog product ID or event relation key, depending on the call.
  • mandant_id, ressource_id: timetable tenant/resource filters.
  • start, stop: call-specific start date and duration; see each call below.
  • max: positive result limit; defaults differ by call.
  • upcoming_only: timetable/alias only; true excludes departures whose departure time has been reached or passed. Off by default.
  • only_available: timetable/alias only; true requests only online-bookable departures with available capacity and omits the visitor availability checkbox. Off by default.
  • newwindow: true opens supported booking links in a new window/tab.
  • show_station: event-calendar selector with true; finder hides departure with false.
  • show_category: event-calendar category selector with true.
  • current_date: finder true initializes today through noon, tomorrow after noon (server time).
  • signets: configured finder signet filter with automatic results.
  • view: call-specific presentation; see below.
  • target: call-specific destination/container; see below.
  • godirect: timetable direct-booking switch or finder destination URL; event calendar uses a URL query instead.
  • title: custom chatbot trigger text or flat-view heading, or booking dialog trigger and heading; not automatically translated.
  • exact: accepted historical attribute with no implemented effect.

All calls below accept the shared account/language/referral/cache context where applicable. Only additional attributes are listed.

timetable / timetablev2

Upcoming departures; both names use the same dispatch. The timetablev2 alias is deprecated for new integrations; use timetable instead. Existing timetablev2 shortcodes remain fully supported. Its name is unrelated to the V2 stylesheet. Unlike Tour finder, this call displays a chronological departure list instead of a departure/destination/date search.

[travelmanager call="timetable" station_id="2" linie_id="146" start="today" stop="3 months" max="12"]

Filters: station_id, linie_id, linie_typ_id, mandant_id, ressource_id. A nonempty linie_typ_id takes precedence over linie_id. Optional: start, stop, max, upcoming_only, only_available, target, godirect, newwindow, view.

Start defaults to today; accepts DD.MM.YYYY or expressions such as next month. Starts older than one month are clamped to today. Stop is a duration from start, e.g. 3 months, without a leading plus; default three months. An invalid/earlier stop falls back to one month. Max defaults to 250; values above 500 also become 250.

Target changes the booking destination; nonempty godirect selects the direct-booking branch. newwindow="true" opens supported links separately. view="ldjson" outputs structured event data without the visible timetable.

Next three available departures today:

[travelmanager call="timetable" start="today" stop="1 day" max="3" upcoming_only="true" only_available="true" newwindow="true"]

Add this example in a WordPress Shortcode block, using straight quotation marks. It uses your saved account; retain an explicit account, station_id or linie_id if your existing integration needs one.

  • start="today": begin with today’s date.
  • stop="1 day": with start=”today”, end at the next local midnight. A departure exactly at midnight belongs to the next day and is excluded.
  • upcoming_only="true" (new): exclude departures whose departure time has already been reached or passed.
  • only_available="true" (new): show only departures the backend reports as online-bookable with available capacity. Visitors do not need to activate a checkbox. The plugin additionally excludes sold-out or unknown-availability rows from the returned data.
  • max="3": with either new filter enabled, show at most three departures after filtering and chronological sorting. Fewer are shown if fewer qualify.
  • newwindow="true": open supported external booking links in a new tab/window.

When no eligible departures remain today, no departure cards are displayed; the existing translated no-results message is shown. Tomorrow’s trips do not fill the list.

The two new options are independent and only the exact value true activates each one. For example, use upcoming_only="true" alone to show future departures while retaining sold-out entries. Use only_available="true" alone to filter availability without adding a current-time cutoff. Other periods still work: retain both filters and change stop="1 day" to stop="1 week" for upcoming available departures within the week starting today.

Both timetable names support the options; other calls ignore them. If neither option is enabled, the previous request, output and cache behavior are preserved. No existing shortcode needs to be changed. The new behavior requires updated plugin and backend versions; adding attributes to an older installation is not an update.

The backend timetablev3 endpoint must support these flags and filter/sort before applying max. The plugin cannot recover candidates omitted by an older backend’s early limit. Remove cancelled trips from online booking in Travelmanager so they are omitted by the endpoint. Opt-in API reads bypass the plugin cache, even with cache=true. Exclude the page from full-page/CDN caches separately. An open page updates on a new render, not continuously.

Tour finder (fahrtfinder2)

Tour finder with AJAX departure/destination/date results.

[travelmanager call="fahrtfinder2" station_id="2" linien_ids="146" current_date="true"]

Optional: station_id, linien_ids, linie_typ_id, signets, max, show_station, current_date, target, godirect. Target is the results element ID; godirect is the result-link destination URL. Max applies to signet results. Signets require backend configuration. Without signets, URL station_id/stop_station_id can preselect stations; URL linien_ids precedes its attribute. Shortcode linie_typ_id precedes URL category_id. No shortcode start-date attribute is implemented here.

calendar

Backend route calendar. Requires linie_id or linie_typ_id.

[travelmanager call="calendar" linie_id="146" station_id="2" start="next month"]

Optional: station_id, start (default this month), newwindow. Dates and booking links come from the backend.

eventcalendar

Event calendar with optional filters. Supply a valid linie_typ_id from your account and the desired station_id. The current backend requires a route type; a station alone can return HTTP 400 (missing route type). The example uses the sandbox IDs 23 and 1: replace them with your own account IDs. Existing plugin validation still accepts either attribute for compatibility with older backends.

[travelmanager call="eventcalendar" linie_typ_id="23" station_id="1" show_station="true" show_category="true"]

Optional: start, show_station, show_category, target, newwindow. Selectors require true; the category selector does not replace the initial linie_typ_id. target="internal" selects internal links. The page query ?godirect=true controls direct navigation. URL station_id/linie_typ_id can override filters. The DE/EN fallback described above applies in opt-in language mode.

booking

Complete V3 trip and ticket selection inside your page, including configured seat, cabin and vehicle modules. Requires a compatible backend with embedding enabled for your website.

[travelmanager call="booking"]
[travelmanager call="booking" view="dialog"]
[travelmanager call="booking" linie_id="7" station_id="4" datum="2026-11-13"]

The default view embeds booking in the page content and grows or shrinks with the complete form, including results and ticket options. Normal website scrolling is used, without a separate iframe scrollbar. view=”dialog” renders a button that opens a modal with a visible header, close control and space around it. Close it using the close control, Escape or the backdrop; focus returns to the button. Closing destroys the instance and reopening starts a fresh view.

Inherits the saved account; explicit account overrides it. Optional presets include linie_id/linien_ids, station_id/hafen_id, stop_station_id/zielhafen_id, datum/date/hinfahrt_datum, rueckfahrt_datum, abfahrt, fahrt, lhf_id, einfache_fahrt, region_id, linie_typ_id, setstyle, onlytarifid, only_betreiber_id, vermittler_id and affiliate_id. Dates accept YYYY-MM-DD, DD.MM.YYYY or Unix seconds. Conflicting aliases are rejected. scroll_offset reserves 0–500 pixels above inline focus/step scroll requests (default 0), without limiting content height. Dialog mode reserves its own margins/header. Optional title labels the dialog trigger and heading; omitted labels use the existing translated booking labels.

Explicit lang overrides a saved fixed plugin language. Automatic mode, and the default legacy setting for this new call, start with the resolved WordPress page language (including WPML/Polylang/page-language filters), with supported browser-language/English fallback. A later page HTML-language change replaces the initial WordPress hint and retains that fallback. Existing calls retain their language behavior.

Loads https://widget.travelmanager.cloud/embed.js once per page and creates a direct iframe from the account’s public shop when the view opens. Inline mode follows the full content height and website scrolling. Dialog mode keeps the iframe within its bounded body and scrolls internally. Website-consent messaging applies to both views. After adding tickets, a one-time-token POST continues the main page to the shop basket and checkout; this flow needs no basket shortcode. The public metadata route never receives the saved WordPress token. Website CSP must allow the widget script/descriptor, shop frame and shop form POST. The account must support the V3 booking/transfer contract; installing this plugin does not update the backend.

After mounting, each [data-tm-booking] element exposes its instance as element.tmBooking for setConsent(…) updates and destroy(); a dialog has this instance only while open. The tm-booking:consent-request event also handles fresh instances after reopening. Publish the updated shared loader alongside this plugin update: WordPress uses its pageLanguage hint and bookingFit content/container sizing. The V3 widget client must support authenticated tm-booking:layout messages for inline scrolling. The plugin ZIP does not publish the hosted loader.

eventinfo

Event details, availability and embedded ticket configuration. Requires product_id or a supported relation URL. Include basket on the same page:

[travelmanager call="basket"]
[travelmanager call="eventinfo" product_id="YOUR_RELATION_KEY" view="list" max="10"]

Optional: view, max. view="list" shows departures for one-way products when dated details exist and the number of available days is within max (default 10); otherwise a calendar appears. Route configuration determines return-trip options. The external service supplies ticket configuration and checkout.

eventcard

Compact event preview with image, teaser, location, optional duration and scheduled departures. Requires product_id as a relation key.

[travelmanager call="eventcard" product_id="YOUR_RELATION_KEY" max="3"]

Optional: max (default 3, capped at 50), newwindow. Book now opens the shared booking dialog for the event’s route and stations, where visitors choose a date and tickets. The original shop URL remains the fallback; newwindow=”true” and custom shop destinations retain direct navigation. Language/referral context is preserved. Referral precedence: URL ref, shortcode vermittler_id, session referral. No prices, reservation or …
sections.installation:
1. Install travelmanager-buchungssoftware and activate it.
  2. Keep existing shortcodes or save an optional default account in Settings → Travelmanager.
  3. Save, then test the endpoint connection.
  4. Optionally select Automatic/fixed language and add Shortcode blocks.
sections.faq:
Must customers change existing pages?

No. Existing accounts, identifiers and legacy language behavior remain supported. New language behavior is opt-in.

How do I add website text to the chatbot?

With a plugin version containing Content Bridge, enable it under Settings → Travelmanager → Settings → Content Bridge and save. Copy the displayed URL into the Travelmanager chatbot’s website-source setting, then update its knowledge. The bridge exports eligible pages and posts as plain text. It is a setting, not a shortcode, and is disabled by default.

Why are timetable or booking results missing from the text export?

The bridge reads saved editorial text and never executes plugin shortcodes or dynamic blocks. Generated timetables, calendars, availability, booking interfaces and other plugin output are deliberately excluded. Drafts, password-protected, private and supported noindex content are excluded too.

How do I show only the next three available departures today?

Use [travelmanager call="timetable" start="today" stop="1 day" max="3" upcoming_only="true" only_available="true" newwindow="true"] after the matching plugin/backend update. Set the WordPress timezone for your departure location. Filtering and sorting happen before the limit, and the interval ends at the next local midnight. With no qualifying departure, the existing no-results message appears rather than tomorrow’s trips. Remove or disable both new options to retain the original behavior.

How do I remove a cancelled departure, and when does the list refresh?

Remove the departure from online booking in the Travelmanager backend (“do not book online”). The endpoint then omits it; no separate cancellation parameter is needed. With either new filter active, the plugin requests fresh API data even with cache=”true”. Separately exclude this page from any page-cache plugin or CDN cache so visitors receive current data. The list updates when the page is opened or reloaded; an already open page does not automatically refresh.

Is a token required?

Only when required by your Travelmanager account. Copy its WordPress token into the optional plugin setting. Without a stored token, legacy requests remain unchanged; a protected account will report an authentication error.

Where are translations maintained?

Frontend dictionaries: libs/dialoge_.php. Settings/status and opt-in corrections: libs/languages/.json. Every changed plugin-owned text must ship in all nine languages together. Customer content is maintained in the booking backend.

Can one page use multiple accounts or languages?

Explicit accounts take precedence. In Automatic/fixed mode, supported lang attributes select each instance’s language, including AJAX and datepicker labels.

How do I customize the appearance or restore the old design?

The Travelmanager settings page has two tabs: Settings (account, optional token, language, connection test and optional Content Bridge) and Layout (style version, colors and preview). Switching tabs retains unsaved input. Content Bridge has its own save button and does not change connection or layout settings.

Open Settings → Travelmanager → Layout. V2 is enabled by default on both existing and new installations. It modernizes plugin forms, cards, calendars, tabs and dialogs while keeping existing shortcode parameters and booking behavior.

The V2 event calendar uses the configured palette, a grouped filter bar and a seven-column month grid. Below 760px of available plugin width it becomes a day-by-day agenda with full tour titles and touch-friendly booking links. Dates, filter requests and booking destinations stay unchanged; the same layout applies after AJAX updates.

Choose V1 and save to restore the previous stylesheet and its saved colors. V2 colors are stored separately and do not change V1. No content migration is required.

V2 provides primary, secondary, surface, text, muted-background and border colors, with a live preview. Leave colors empty to use supported theme variables (WordPress primary/secondary presets, Elementor global colors and Avada’s primary fallback) or neutral defaults. The theme’s font is inherited. Button text automatically switches between light and dark for the chosen accent. Custom text/background combinations still need a contrast check.

Colors affect only Travelmanager elements, including its own jQuery UI popups. They do not change the WordPress theme, admin controls, other plugins or external booking iframe contents. The preview uses the admin font; review the final result on your website. Reset colors clears V2 overrides, preserves your selected style version and leaves account/token settings and V1 colors unchanged. Clear any full-page/CDN cache after changing appearance.

Use only_available="true" alone to filter availability without adding a current-time cutoff. Other periods still work: retain both filters and change stop="1 day" to stop="1 week" for upcoming available departures within the week starting today.

Both timetable names support the options; other calls ignore them. If neither option is enabled, the previous request, output and cache behavior are preserved. No existing shortcode needs to be changed. The new behavior requires updated plugin and backend versions; adding attributes to an older installation is not an update.

The backend timetablev3 endpoint must support these flags and filter/sort before applying max. The plugin cannot recover candidates omitted by an older backend’s early limit. Remove cancelled trips from online booking in Travelmanager so they are omitted by the endpoint. Opt-in API reads bypass the plugin cache, even with cache=true. Exclude the page from full-page/CDN caches separately. An open page updates on a new render, not continuously.

Tour finder (fahrtfinder2)

Tour finder with AJAX departure/destination/date results.

[travelmanager call="fahrtfinder2" station_id="2" linien_ids="146" current_date="true"]

Optional: station_id, linien_ids, linie_typ_id, signets, max, show_station, current_date, target, godirect. Target is the results element ID; godirect is the result-link destination URL. Max applies to signet results. Signets require backend configuration. Without signets, URL station_id/stop_station_id can preselect stations; URL linien_ids precedes its attribute. Shortcode linie_typ_id precedes URL category_id. No shortcode start-date attribute is implemented here.

calendar

Backend route calendar. Requires linie_id or linie_typ_id.

[travelmanager call="calendar" linie_id="146" station_id="2" start="next month"]

Optional: station_id, start (default this month), newwindow. Dates and booking links come from the backend.

eventcalendar

Event calendar with optional filters. Supply a valid linie_typ_id from your account and the desired station_id. The current backend requires a route type; a station alone can return HTTP 400 (missing route type). The example uses the sandbox IDs 23 and 1: replace them with your own account IDs. Existing plugin validation still accepts either attribute for compatibility with older backends.

[travelmanager call="eventcalendar" linie_typ_id="23" station_id="1" show_station="true" show_category="true"]

Optional: start, show_station, show_category, target, newwindow. Selectors require true; the category selector does not replace the initial linie_typ_id. target="internal" selects internal links. The page query ?godirect=true controls direct navigation. URL station_id/linie_typ_id can override filters. The DE/EN fallback described above applies in opt-in language mode.

booking

Complete V3 trip and ticket selection inside your page, including configured seat, cabin and vehicle modules. Requires a compatible backend with embedding enabled for your website.

[travelmanager call="booking"]
[travelmanager call="booking" view="dialog"]
[travelmanager call="booking" linie_id="7" station_id="4" datum="2026-11-13"]

The default view embeds booking in the page content and grows or shrinks with the complete form, including results and ticket options. Normal website scrolling is used, without a separate iframe scrollbar. view=”dialog” renders a button that opens a modal with a visible header, close control and space around it. Close it using the close control, Escape or the backdrop; focus returns to the button. Closing destroys the instance and reopening starts a fresh view.

Inherits the saved account; explicit account overrides it. Optional presets include linie_id/linien_ids, station_id/hafen_id, stop_station_id/zielhafen_id, datum/date/hinfahrt_datum, rueckfahrt_datum, abfahrt, fahrt, lhf_id, einfache_fahrt, region_id, linie_typ_id, setstyle, onlytarifid, only_betreiber_id, vermittler_id and affiliate_id. Dates accept YYYY-MM-DD, DD.MM.YYYY or Unix seconds. Conflicting aliases are rejected. scroll_offset reserves 0–500 pixels above inline focus/step scroll requests (default 0), without limiting content height. Dialog mode reserves its own margins/header. Optional title labels the dialog trigger and heading; omitted labels use the existing translated booking labels.

Explicit lang overrides a saved fixed plugin language. Automatic mode, and the default legacy setting for this new call, start with the resolved WordPress page language (including WPML/Polylang/page-language filters), with supported browser-language/English fallback. A later page HTML-language change replaces the initial WordPress hint and retains that fallback. Existing calls retain their language behavior.

Loads https://widget.travelmanager.cloud/embed.js once per page and creates a direct iframe from the account’s public shop when the view opens. Inline mode follows the full content height and website scrolling. Dialog mode keeps the iframe within its bounded body and scrolls internally. Website-consent messaging applies to both views. After adding tickets, a one-time-token POST continues the main page to the shop basket and checkout; this flow needs no basket shortcode. The public metadata route never receives the saved WordPress token. Website CSP must allow the widget script/descriptor, shop frame and shop form POST. The account must support the V3 booking/transfer contract; installing this plugin does not update the backend.

After mounting, each [data-tm-booking] element exposes its instance as element.tmBooking for setConsent(…) updates and destroy(); a dialog has this instance only while open. The tm-booking:consent-request event also handles fresh instances after reopening. Publish the updated shared loader alongside this plugin update: WordPress uses its pageLanguage hint and bookingFit content/container sizing. The V3 widget client must support authenticated tm-booking:layout messages for inline scrolling. The plugin ZIP does not publish the hosted loader.

eventinfo

Event details, availability and embedded ticket configuration. Requires product_id or a supported relation URL. Include basket on the same page:

[travelmanager call="basket"]
[travelmanager call="eventinfo" product_id="YOUR_RELATION_KEY" view="list" max="10"]

Optional: view, max. view="list" shows departures for one-way products when dated details exist and the number of available days is within max (default 10); otherwise a calendar appears. Route configuration determines return-trip options. The external service supplies ticket configuration and checkout.

eventcard

Compact event preview with image, teaser, location, optional duration and scheduled departures. Requires product_id as a relation key.

[travelmanager call="eventcard" product_id="YOUR_RELATION_KEY" max="3"]

Optional: max (default 3, capped at 50), newwindow. Book now opens the shared booking dialog for the event’s route and stations, where visitors choose a date and tickets. The original shop URL remains the fallback; newwindow=”true” and custom shop destinations retain direct navigation. Language/referral context is preserved. Referral precedence: URL ref, shortcode vermittler_id, session referral. No prices, reservation or …

upgrade_notice.22.41: V2 styling becomes active automatically, including on existing pages. Select V1 in Settings → Travelmanager to restore the previous design. Existing shortcodes and default language behavior remain supported. New language modes are optional. Test session-dependent booking pages before rollout.
